caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 579 of 2010.
lawyer:
For Petitioners: Mr. S. N. Goswami, Advocate, instructed by Mr. Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record. 
For the Respondents: Not represented.
parties:
Md. Amirul Islam ------ Petitioner
Versus
The State and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. Muhammad Imman Ali, J: This Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 12.10.2010 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.23291 of 2009 discharging the Rule. 

 2. The relevant facts, for disposal of the case, are that respondent No.2, Enamul Haque lodged First Information Report with Dhamoirhat Police Station, Naogaon against the petitioner alleging inter alia that the petitioner as Member of the . Managing Committee of Dhamoirhat M. M. Degree College approached the informant (respondent No.2 herein) saying that if he could pay Tk.70,000/- for the development of the College, he would be appointed as Assistant Accountant of the College. In view of such assurance, the informant paid Tk.70,000/- to the petitioner for the said purpose. Accordingly, the petitioner managed an appointment letter for the said post on 23.9.2001. But subsequently, it transpires that there was no such post in the College and as such, no salary could ever be paid to the respondent No.2 against the fake appointment letter. Subsequently respondent No.2 demanded return of the money. Then the petitioner gave a hand note dated 10.5.2007 with undertaking that he would return the money, but ultimately he did not do so. As such the F.I.R. was lodged against the petitioner. 

 4. Thereafter, the case was transmitted to the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate. The learned Judge of the said Court framed charge against the petitioner under Sections 420/406 of the Penal Code. 

 7. Mr. S. N. Goswami, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the petitioner submitted that the informant alleged in the FIR that he gave Tk.70,000/- to the petitioner for development works of the college and as such the proceeding 'against the petitioner under Sections 420/406 of the Penal Code ate an abuse of the process of the Court. He further submitted that the informant admitted in the FIR that he was given appointment as Assistant Accountant and, therefore, there cannot be 'any criminal liability and hence the High Court Division erred in discharging the Rule. He finally submitted that clearly the informant did not make out any case of cheating under Sections `420/406 of the Penal Code, and there was no question of any entrustment and hence, if at all, there may be a civil liability and as such the criminal proceedings are an abuse of the process of the Court and should be quashed. In support of his contention the learned Advocate has referred to an unreported decision of this 'Division dated 17 November, 2013 in Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No.235 of 2013. In that case a sum of money was paid to an official of the bank by way of loan and also a sum of money was encashed by the hank using the undated cheques signed by the complainant of that case. The learned Advocate submitted that since in that case this Division did not entertain the Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal on the ground that the money paid over to the accused was by way of loan, similarly in the instant case when the money was paid over for development works, there can be no criminal liability. 

 10. The facts of the case referred by the learned Advocate for the petitioner are quite  different' from the facts of the instant case, inasmuch as in the case referred the informant had stated that the money was handed over on various dates as loan and the money drawn by way of cheques was for bank interest on the loan. In the instant case the money was taken in the name of development works and for giving the informant a job. Purportedly the informant was appointed as an Assistant Accountant, but in reality no such post existed and the informant did not receive salary for a long time and upon inquiry found out that the post, for which he had been appointed, did not exist. Moreover, it appears that the accused, when confronted by the informant agreed to return the sum of Tk.70,000/- and on 10.05.2007 at 12.45 p.m. at Dhamoirhat Bazar, gave an undertaking by way of a hand note in presence of one Abdul Mukit. 

 11. The High Court Division observed that there is a specific allegation against the accused petitioner, who induced the informant to pay Tk.70,000/- to get a job in the college in a fraudulent manner and did not return the money and, therefore, evidently ingredient of cheating and criminal breach of trust exist calling for initiation of a criminal proceeding. It was further observed that the Investigating Officer also found truth in the allegation and accordingly submitted charge sheet in the 'case to proceed against the accused petitioner.
